The datasheet is modelled, for the reasons in provenance - the sibling's datasheet states the same triple independently, 438.4 is the body width this vendor's 1RU line uses, and the figure's own aspect prefers it - but the quick-start is not wrong for being outvoted, and the same conflict stands unresolved on agr130, which shares that quick-start. A tape measure on a real unit settles it in one minute.","what":"chassis-dimensions"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"The six QSFP28 ports are numbered 48 to 53 here on the strength of the vendor's zero-based scheme, not on a reading. No figure held resolves their numerals: the quick-start's section 6 zoom crops that end of the faceplate away and the datasheet render prints the band under its own callout highlighting. Which column is the lower number, and whether the separate bottom row continues the sequence or precedes it, need a straight-on photograph of the right-hand end of the front panel.","what":"qsfp-port-numbering"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"The bezel between the upper QSFP block's two rows carries FOUR marks per column where the SFP+ bezel carries two. That is either two lamps per port or a four-lane column serving one of them, and 9.1 px/mm cannot separate those. One lamp per port is drawn; the other two marks per column are not. A photograph of one QSFP shell at better than 9 px/mm settles it.","what":"qsfp-lamp-count"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"The quick-start's section 6 zoom draws PS0, PS1, Diag, Fan and Loc as text INSIDE a light rectangle, which reads as a legend printed on the lens rather than beside it - unlike Reset, two centimetres away on the same band, which is plain white text on the chassis. It is drawn here as a lamp with its legend over it. Whether the real part prints on the lens or beside it is a bench photograph.","what":"system-led-legend-placement"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"The management jack's link and activity lamps are BELOW THE CONSOLE PORT, not in the jack - a reader with better photographs than this corpus holds sees them there, which is why the jack is modelled on the bare std/rj45-ganged@2 rather than the lamped Ethernet cell. They are now placed, straddling the `Mgmt` label at 409.30 and 420.20 mm, from a reader looking at the hardware. The datasheet render does not resolve them on its own - the band carries marks at 407.88, 409.63 and 410.73 mm and a brighter one at 30.1 to 31.0, and at 9.1 px/mm nothing separates a lamp from a legend among them - so the positions bracket the label rather than landing on a measured mark. What remains open is only the exact offset either side.","what":"management-port-lamps"},{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["front"],"wanted":"Twenty-six lamps on this face carry a legend printed on the lens: the twenty-four lane lamps their lane number 0 to 3, and the two management lamps `LNK` and `ACT` - legible in a close photograph of the hardware. It is not drawn, and the obstacle is the model rather than the evidence: the renderer paints a placement over its own silkscreen, so ink at a lamp's centre is invisible and L21 says so, and there is nowhere else for it to go - the port numerals sit 0.8 mm above the lamp row and the label bar directly below it. The same is true of the five system-LED legends at the other end of the face. What would fix both is a way for a lamp to carry a legend on its own lens, which is a component or renderer question and not this device's to answer.","what":"uplink-lane-lamp-numerals"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"The two grounding points do not look alike. Callout 7 points to a single round opening at the lower left, about 7.9 mm; the right-hand end carries a light plate with two holes one above the other, 424.7 to 436.7 mm, which matches the quick-start's \"One grounding lug, 2 M5 screws\" kit. Both are drawn with common/ground-lug@1. Whether the left-hand one is a second lug pad, a single bonding screw, or something else is a photograph of the rear left corner.","what":"rear-grounding-points"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"5+1","redundancy-note":"hot-swappable 5+1 redundant fan modules"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"leds":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster - the out-of-band 100/1000BASE-T RJ-45 and the RS-232 console share one ganged bezel at the right-hand end of the faceplate, and the USB-A storage port sits apart from them in the silkscreen band. Three media, one job: reaching and disciplining the box rather than carrying its traffic. The Reset button is counted here for the same reason.","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"index-origin":0,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"2 redundant, load-sharing, hot-swappable AC or -48 VDC"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp28","speed":"100g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp-plus":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","lint":{"waive":{"L61":"led-qsfp-50-51-2 sits 1.62 mm left of the centre of the two ports it serves, and so it should: it is one of FOUR lamps in a cluster, and only a two-lamp set could have a member on the centreline. All four positions are read off the figure. Lane 2 is simply the one that lands inside the rule's window; the other three are further off and do not trip it. Centring it would move a lamp off its measurement to quieten a rule, which is the trade this repository does not make.","L76":"The management jack is an Ethernet jack on a part with no lamps, and that is the point: its link and activity lamps are not in the jack. They sit BELOW THE CONSOLE PORT, two rows down from the housing they serve, reported by a reader looking at the hardware. Putting it on common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 would draw two lamps in the cell's outer corners where the metal has none, which is the defect this rule exists to prevent, one level up. docs/rj45-family-design.md lists five ways the library expresses jack lamps and names \"deliberately left undrawn (the S6301 pair's stated position)\" as one of them; this is that case, and the position is stated in `management-port-lamps`. ufispace/s6301-56stp models the same arrangement - bare std/rj45-ganged@2 plus separate lamps - and escapes this rule only by omitting `media` from the placement, which hides the media rather than declaring it. Declaring rj45 and waiving the rule is the more honest of the two. Delete this waiver when a photograph resolves the lamps and they can be placed."}},"manufacturer":"Edgecore","maturity":"modelled","model":"AS5916-54XL","name":"agr110","portfolio":{"family":"Aggregation Router","line":"Service Provider","series":"AGR110"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"airflow":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - EVERY ordering code published for this model ends in -F: 5916-54XL-O-AC-F and its regional variants, 5916-54XL-O-48V-F, and the -OT- extended-temperature pairs. So only front-to-back SKUs are listed, and the trays in the figure print F2B. The quick-start describes both directions in general terms - \"All installed modules must have a front-to-back (F2B) airflow direction, or all modules must have a back-to-front (B2F) airflow direction\" - but that is the family's caution, not an ordering code, and no B2F part number appears. Configurations here are therefore ac and dc, both front-to-back, and the absence of a B2F SKU is stated rather than assumed away."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - \"Dimensions (WxDxH): 438.4 x 501.9 x 44 mm (17.26 x 19.76 x 1.73 in)\" (agr110-datasheet/doc.md:109). THE TWO DOCUMENTS DISAGREE and the disagreement is recorded in gaps as sources-disagree: the shared quick-start's hardware specification says \"435 x 515 x 43.84 mm\" (agr110-qsg/doc.md, Switch Chassis / Size), which differs on all three axes, 13 mm of it in depth. The datasheet is taken for three reasons. The SIBLING's datasheet states the same triple independently - agr130-datasheet/doc.md:103 is \"438.4 x 501.9 x 44 mm\" to the digit - so two documents state it and one states the other. 438.4 is the body width the rest of this vendor's 1RU line uses and is already the metal between the ear folds, the same figure dcs510 and cor580 carry, so nothing is subtracted here and the rack ears are optional placements outside it at the library's 14 mm. And the figure prefers it: the rear panel's measured aspect of 10.18 sits nearer 9.96 (438.4/44) than 9.92 (435/43.84). The weights do not disagree - 9.7 kg against 9.72 - so this is not two different products."},"chassis-colour":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"photo - the chassis is black with a dark grey faceplate. Both panels of agr110-datasheet/fig-0009 and all three stock photographs agree. The quick-start's line art draws a light-grey shell and is the odd one out, as it is on dcs510; where the guide art and the device disagree the device wins."},"figure-choice":{"confidence":"measured","note":"Gate 1, and the prepared brief's ranked candidates were NOT used. prepare.py ranks the docling-extracted figures, whose best here is agr110-datasheet/fig-0009 at 3.29 px/mm. The same figure taken off a 600 dpi render of its own page (pdftocairo -png -r 600 -f 2) measures at 9.12 px/mm, nearly three times the resolution, and that is what every number below was read at. Panel boxes found by row/column darkness: FRONT (382,1728)-(4389,2120), 4008 x 393 px; REAR (386,2824)-(4385,3216), 4000 x 393 px. The two agree on width to 0.2 percent, which is what anchors the x scale at 9.124 px/mm on 438.4 mm. THE FIGURE IS A RENDER, NOT A DRAWING, and its aspect says so: 10.18 against 9.96 for 438.4/44, 2.1 percent out. The tell is not the arithmetic but the art - the TOP cage row shows more of its interior than the bottom row does, which happens when the camera sits slightly above the face. 2.1 percent is inside the four percent at which docs/modelling-a-device.md still allows fractions, so: x carries geometry directly, and every y here is either a proportion of the panel's own 393 px height mapped onto 44 mm or a registry figure anchored on one such proportion. No absolute vertical measurement was taken from this image. THE QUICK START GUIDE'S ART WAS REJECTED. Its page-1 front elevation measures 1199 x 148 px - aspect 8.10 against 9.96, NINETEEN percent out, vertically stretched - and docs/modelling-a-device.md says that at ten percent you cannot take absolute scale at all. It puts the inter-row LED bezel at 17.24 mm where the datasheet render puts it at 15.17. The guide also disclaims itself in its own words, on page 1: \"The switch drawings in this document are for illustration only and may not match your particular switch model.\" So the QSG is used here for TEXT ONLY - the specification table, the power ratings, and the section 6 zoom, which is a photograph of the real faceplate rather than line art."},"management-cluster":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured - the RJ-45 management port above the RJ-45 console port, in ONE white bezel running 406.79 to 424.18 mm, centre 415.49. The row centres read 9.1 and 21.2 mm, a pitch of 12.1 - which is `rj45-ganged`'s own measured row pitch of 12.1 to the millimetre, and that is what identifies the pair as a GANGED 2x1 block rather than two single jacks: a single jack's housing is 15.8 x 13.2 and two of those cannot sit 12.1 apart. The rows are mirrored, not translated - the upper jack's keyway points up and the lower jack's down, visible in the datasheet figure at 9.1 px/mm - which is the ganged form's normal construction and the reason the top row carries rotate 180. THE LEGEND IS READ AT LAST, off a close photograph of the hardware: `(up) Mgmt` on one line and `(down) Console` beneath it, in the band under the jacks - the same up/down idiom this faceplate uses for every stacked pair. Three drafts could not read it. The first invented `Mgmt (up)(down) Console` from dcs510's one-line idiom and was removed for saying what nobody had seen; the second measured three lines of ink at 401-420 mm and recorded that it could not resolve them; this one has the words. They are drawn, at the measured line spans - 404.0-418.1 for the first and 404.0-419.9 for the second. THE MANAGEMENT JACK'S LAMPS ARE NOT IN THE JACK, and they do not straddle its label either - a close photograph of the hardware shows the block as three stacked rows: `(up) Mgmt`, then the two lamps side by side beneath it, then `(down) Console`. They are labelled LNK and ACT on their own lenses, which is what settles their vocabulary: link on one and activity on the other, both green, exactly the `off / link / activity` split docs/rj45-family-design.md states as the family default and which a bare jack could not carry. Drawn with those states. An earlier draft put them left and right of the whole label, which is where a first reading of a low-resolution figure had suggested; the photograph says between the lines - off the connector entirely, two rows down from the jack they serve. So the management jack takes the BARE std/rj45-ganged@2 rather than common/rj45-ganged-eth@1, whose whole difference is two lamps in the cell's outer corners; drawing those would put lit hardware on a housing that has none. This is the S6301 arrangement exactly - ufispace/s6301-56stp's own provenance describes \"the OOB management jack (two lamps above it)\" and models it as a bare std/rj45-ganged@2 with two separate common/led-dot placements carrying `for: mgmt`. The difference here is that the S6301's HIG resolves its lamp positions at 3.13 px/mm and this datasheet render does not: the band under the console jack carries small marks at 407.88, 409.63 and 410.73 mm between y 27.4 and 28.6, and nothing at 9.1 px/mm separates a lamp from a legend among them. So the lamps are recorded as a gap rather than placed, which is the fourth of the five treatments docs/rj45-family-design.md lists - deliberately undrawn, position stated."},"port-block-layout":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured - THREE ganged blocks of eight columns by two rows, 48 ports. The blocks were found from the top bezel lip (the continuous bright band at y 1.5-2.8 mm, which runs the length of a ganged bezel and stops in the gap between blocks): 13.78..127.32, 130.49..243.70 and 246.44..362.16 mm, widths 113.54, 113.21 and 115.72. Eight ports at the registry pitch is 114.0 and SFF-8433's own 1xN bezel cutout is N x 14.25 + 1.2 = 115.2, so the three measured widths bracket the standard's own figure and the block count is not in doubt. Block pitch reads 116.71 and 115.95, mean 116.33, against SFF-8433's C04 block-to-block minimum extrapolated to 1x8 of 116.5."},"port-leds":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured - ONE lamp per port, an outline triangle, both lamps of a column sharing the white bezel between the two rows: the upper port's points up and sits left of the column centre, the lower port's points down and sits right of it. Read in agr110-qsg's section 6 zoom, which resolves the pair inside each bezel cell, and confirmed in agr110-datasheet/fig-0009 where each cell carries two marks about 3.9 mm apart. The lamps are drawn with common/led-arrow@1's up and down skins at +/- 1.95 mm from the column centre. THIS NEEDED A TOOL CHANGE. expand.py could offset a block's lamps by their position within a gang (`dx-by-col`) but not by their ROW, which is the only thing that distinguishes these two - one y, two x. `dx-by-row` was added to the lamp block for it, mirroring the knob the numerals already had for exactly the same reason on faces that print `n (up)(down) n+1`."},"port-numbering":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing, and this one is read rather than inferred. agr110-qsg's section 6 zoom prints, under the first four columns, \"0(up-triangle) (down-triangle)1 2(up) (down)3 4(up) (down)5 6(up) (down)7\". So NUMBERING STARTS AT ZERO, EVEN PORTS ARE THE TOP ROW and odd the bottom, numbered along the face in column pairs, and the solid triangle beside each numeral names its row. 48 ports are 0..47. The numeral glyphs measure at 17.61-19.69 and 22.42-24.50 mm under the first column (centre 21.52), so they sit about 3 mm either side of their column centre with the triangle pair between them, on one baseline at 29.6 mm. Note what this settles for the whole line: it is the same `n (up)(down) n+1` idiom dcs510 prints, but ZERO-BASED, and the datasheet's sibling DCS500 says in words that \"port, fan and PSU numbering start at zero\"."},"port-pitch":{"confidence":"registry","note":"registry, not measured, per the rule that a ganged pitch is a lookup. spec/schemas/standards.yaml `sfp-ganged` states 14.25 as SFF-8433's B04 Basic - a dimension with no tolerance - with the 14.25 x 10.40 per-port opening and a measured 15.0 belly-to-belly row pitch. What this figure measures is 14.0 to 14.5 column to column, and across the eight columns of the first block the fitted pitch is 14.110 against the standard's 14.25. That one percent is the FIGURE's scale error, not the cage's: a render whose aspect is already 2.1 percent out is not evidence against an SFF Basic dimension. The blocks are therefore laid out on 14.25 and anchored so the region as a whole lands where it was measured - first column centre 21.52 against a measured 21.33, last column centre 354.44 against a measured 354.34 - which leaves a residue of up to 1.2 mm in the middle of each block. That residue is the price of taking the standard over the render and it is recorded rather than hidden. Gutter 2.59 is what makes the two ends land: 23 steps of 14.25 plus two gutters over the measured span."},"port-rows":{"confidence":"registry","note":"registry, anchored on one measured proportion. The white bezel band that runs between the two cage rows centres at 15.17 mm of the panel's height (bright band 13.44-16.91, read as a fraction of the 393 px panel). With `sfp-ganged`'s measured 15.0 row pitch that puts the top row's centre at 7.67 and the bottom row's at 22.67, openings 10.40 tall. The check is the block's outer extent: the modelled openings span 2.47 to 27.87 mm and the figure's outer bezel lips run 1.23 to 28.2, so the bezel stands about 1.2 mm proud of the opening at the top and 0.3 at the bottom - an asymmetry which is the camera, not the metal, and which is why no row was measured directly."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet and quick-start together. The BOX figure is \"Power Consumption - 450 Watts maximum\" (agr110-qsg/doc.md), unqualified as to scope, so it is recorded as power-max-w with power-envelope unstated. Input ratings are the quick-start's: AC \"100-240 VAC, 50-60 Hz, 6 A maximum\", DC \"-36 - -72 VDC, 28-14 A\"; the datasheet gives the ranges without the currents. NO PER-MODULE POWER IS PUBLISHED. Searched both documents for the field name rather than the part number - \"Power\", \"Consumption\", \"Watt\", \"PSU\" - and neither states an output rating for a supply or a draw for a fan tray, which is the same silence the AS7946 parts found across the same vendor's corpus. common/psu-ac-650@3 carries its own 650 W output from the chassis that do state it; the fan trays carry nothing and L27 stands on them, which is the record that the figure is missing rather than guessed."},"qsfp-block":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured, and it is NOT one block. The six QSFP28 ports are a 2x2 stacked ganged block with a lamp bezel between its rows, and a SEPARATE 1x2 row below it, which the datasheet's callout-2 highlight encloses together as \"6 x QSFP28 ports\". Column centres read 373.81 and 392.62 mm in both the upper and the lower openings - a pitch of 18.81 against the registry's 19.0 for `qsfp-ganged`, which is the same one percent the SFP+ columns show and is treated the same way. Row centres read 7.5, 23.7 and 36.8: the upper pair are 16.2 apart with their bezel measured at 15.62 between them, and the third row sits 13.1 below the second with no bezel between, which is what makes it a separate block rather than a third row of the same one. The bottom vent band stops at 363.5 mm and does not run under this block, which is consistent with a third row of cages reaching to 41.6."},"qsfp-numbering":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"NOT READ - ASSUMED. The QSFP28 ports are numbered 48 to 53 here, continuing the SFP+ block, because that is what the vendor's zero-based scheme implies and because no figure held here resolves their numerals: the quick-start's section 6 zoom crops the right-hand end of the faceplate away, and at 9.1 px/mm the datasheet render prints their band under the callout highlighting. It is recorded as a gap. Which of the two columns is the lower number, and whether the separate bottom row continues the sequence or precedes it, are the same question and have the same answer: a photograph."},"rear-grounding":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - callout 7 of agr110-datasheet/fig-0009 names a grounding screw and points to a round opening at the lower left of the rear face, at about 7.9 mm. A second point sits at the right-hand end, outboard of PS1 at 424.7 to 436.7 mm: a light plate carrying TWO holes one above the other, which is what the quick-start's own packing list implies - \"Grounding kit - One grounding lug, 2 M5 screws and 2 washers (for AC model)\" is a two-hole lug. The two are drawn alike with common/ground-lug@1 and they do not look alike in the figure; that difference is recorded as a gap rather than resolved by choosing."},"rear-layout":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured - PSU, six fan trays, PSU, with a grounding point outboard of each supply.
